answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Slashing. Each identity must sign a random challenge derived from a fresh global seed. A clone family, sharing one key or seed, can only answer with identical responses, which fail when the expected answer depends on private per-instance state. Honest agents update through a hidden local lagoon of entropy, so their answers diverge naturally. An attacker cloning N identities makes one ripple that exposes all copies at once. Forfeiting one instance reveals its siblings, so the per-identity cost is losing the entire ocean of provisioned instances on first detection.
